paragraphs.text: Καὶ Ἑνὼχ πορευθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Ἀζαήλ· Πορεύου, οὐκ ἔσται σοι εἰρήνη· κρῖμα μέγα ἐξῆλθεν κατὰ σοῦ τοῦ δῆσαί σε.
paragraphs.translit: Kai Henōch poreutheis eipen tō Azaēl; Poreuou, ouk estai soi eirēnē; krima mega exēlthen kata sou tou dēsai se.

i18n.en: And Enoch went and said to Asael: Go, there shall be no peace for you. A great sentence has gone forth against you, to bind you.

notes.official: Enoch delivers the divine-rejection to Asael at Dudael. The rejection-of-petition framework: the Watchers have transgressed beyond clemency-possibility; their fate is fixed for the day of the great judgement. The narrative continues the Asael-as-archetypal-scapegoat tradition documented at central entry `watchers-bound-dudael-azazel-1-enoch-10-lev-16-yom-kippur-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἄνεσις καὶ ἐρώτησις οὐκ ἔσται σοι περὶ ὧν ὑπέδειξας ἀδικιῶν, καὶ περὶ πασῶν τῶν ἀδικιῶν καὶ τῆς ἀσεβείας καὶ ἁμαρτίας ὅσα ὑπέδειξας τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
paragraphs.translit: kai anesis kai erōtēsis ouk estai soi peri hōn hypedeixas adikiōn, kai peri pasōn tōn adikiōn kai tēs asebeias kai hamartias hosa hypedeixas tois anthrōpois.

i18n.en: And there shall be no respite or petition granted to you on account of the unrighteous things you have shown — on account of all the unrighteousness and ungodliness and sin which you have shown to mankind.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐλάλησα πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς ὁμοῦ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν πάντες, καὶ τρόμος καὶ φόβος ἐπέλαβον αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai poreutheis elalēsa pasin autois homou, kai ephobēthēsan pantes, kai tromos kai phobos epelabon autous.

i18n.en: And I went and spoke to them all together, and they were all afraid, and trembling and fear took hold of them.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἠρώτησάν με γράψαι αὐτοῖς ἐρωτήσεως ὑπόμνημα, ἵνα γένηται αὐτοῖς ἄφεσις, καὶ ἵνα ἀναγάγω τὸ ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἐρωτήσεως αὐτῶν ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ērōtēsan me grapsai autois erōtēseōs hypomnēma, hina genētai autois aphesis, kai hina anagagō to hypomnēma tēs erōtēseōs autōn enōpion tou kyriou tou ouranou.

i18n.en: And they asked me to write a memorial of petition for them, that they might find forgiveness, and that I might bring the memorial of their petition before the Lord of heaven.

paragraphs.text: Διότι αὐτοὶ οὐκέτι ἠδύναντο λαλῆσαι οὐδὲ ἐπᾶραι τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀπὸ αἰσχύνης περὶ ὧν ἡμάρτοσαν καὶ ὧν κατεκρίθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: Dioti autoi ouketi ēdynanto lalēsai oude eparai tous ophthalmous autōn eis ton ouranon apo aischynēs peri hōn hēmartosan kai hōn katekrithēsan.

i18n.en: For they themselves could no longer speak, nor lift up their eyes to heaven, for shame on account of the sins they had committed and for which they had been condemned.

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἔγραψα τὸ ὑπόμνημα τῆς ἐρωτήσεως αὐτῶν καὶ τὰς δεήσεις τῶν πνευμάτων αὐτῶν περὶ ἑκάστου ἔργου αὐτῶν καὶ περὶ ὧν ἠρώτουν, ἵνα γένηται αὐτοῖς ἄφεσις καὶ μακρότης.
paragraphs.translit: Tote egrapsa to hypomnēma tēs erōtēseōs autōn kai tas deēseis tōn pneumatōn autōn peri hekastou ergou autōn kai peri hōn ērōtoun, hina genētai autois aphesis kai makrotēs.

i18n.en: Then I wrote out the memorial of their petition, and the prayers of their spirits, concerning each of their deeds and what they asked — that they might have forgiveness and length of days.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐκάθισα ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα Δαν τὰ ἐν Δάν, τὰ ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ Ἑρμωνιεὶμ τὰ πρὸς δυσμάς, καὶ ἀνεγίνωσκον τὸ ὑπόμνημα τῶν δεήσεων αὐτῶν μέχρι οὗ ἐκοιμήθην.
paragraphs.translit: Kai poreutheis ekathisa epi ta hydata Dan ta en Dan, ta ek dexiōn tou Hermōnieim ta pros dysmas, kai aneginōskon to hypomnēma tōn deēseōn autōn mechri hou ekoimēthēn.

i18n.en: And I went and sat down by the waters of Dan, in the land of Dan, to the south-west of Hermon, and I read their memorial of petition until I fell asleep.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ὁράματα ἤρχοντο, καὶ ὁπτασίαι ἐπ' ἐμοῦ ἔπιπτον, καὶ τὰς βλεφαρίδας τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν μου ἐπὶ τὰς πύλας τοῦ παλατίου ἐπέλαβον.
paragraphs.translit: Kai idou horamata ērchonto, kai optasiai ep' emou epipton, kai tas blepharidas tōn ophthalmōn mou epi tas pylas tou palatiou epelabon.

i18n.en: And behold, dreams came upon me, and visions fell upon me, and I saw visions of the great judgment in my eyes — and a voice came to me, saying: Speak to the sons of heaven, that they may be rebuked.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐλάλησα πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς ὁμοῦ, καὶ συνήχθησαν πάντες πενθοῦντες ἐν Ἀβελ-σεγαὴλ, ἥ ἐστιν μεταξὺ Λιβάνου καὶ Σενεσὲρ, κεκαλυμμένοι τοῖς προσώποις.
paragraphs.translit: Kai poreutheis elalēsa pasin autois homou, kai synēchthēsan pantes penthountes en Abel-segaēl, hē estin metaxy Libanou kai Seneser, kekalymmenoi tois prosōpois.

i18n.en: And when I awoke, I went to them, and they were all gathered together in mourning at Abel-segael, which is between Lebanon and Senesēr, with their faces covered.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐλάλησα ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν πάντα τὰ ὁράματα ἃ εἶδον ἐν τῷ ὕπνῳ, καὶ ἠρξάμην λαλεῖν τοὺς λόγους τῆς δικαιοσύνης, καὶ κατὰ τῶν Ἐγρηγόρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπιτιμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai elalēsa enōpion autōn panta ta horamata ha eidon en tō hypnō, kai ērxamēn lalein tous logous tēs dikaiosynēs, kai kata tōn Egrēgorōn tou ouranou epitimōn.

i18n.en: And I told them all the visions which I had seen in my sleep, and I began to speak the words of righteousness, and to rebuke the Watchers of heaven.
